key_insight: The paper shows that frozen LLM embeddings are not naturally multilingual: sentences with the same meaning can land in different regions depending on language. By removing paired language-specific residual subspaces, the authors improve multilingual alignment without training.
problem_solved: It addresses the lack of effective multilingual, training-free text embeddings from frozen LLMs. Existing methods are mostly English-centric and struggle when semantically equivalent texts in different languages produce mismatched embeddings.
method: Systematically analyze embedding geometry across languages to identify language-conditioned misalignment.
Estimate paired language-specific residual subspaces that capture non-semantic variation.
Remove these residual directions from embeddings to improve cross-lingual semantic alignment without model fine-tuning.
impact: This gives practitioners a lightweight way to obtain better multilingual embeddings from frozen LLMs, reducing the need for extra training or multilingual supervision. It can improve cross-lingual retrieval, clustering, and evaluation pipelines that rely on semantically consistent embeddings.
visual_elements: A cross-lingual embedding space plot showing misaligned sentence pairs before and after correction.
A subspace decomposition diagram highlighting semantic vs. language-specific residual components.
A pipeline graphic: frozen LLM -> embedding extraction -> paired-residual removal -> improved multilingual embeddings.
A comparison chart of retrieval or alignment scores across languages before vs. after the method.
paper_title: Steering beyond Language: Improving Multilingual Training-Free Text Embeddings via Paired-Residual Subspace Removal
paper_authors: Ailiang Lin, Zhuoyun Li, Yusong Wang, Keyu Mao, Kotaro Funakoshi
